title: Une approche hilbertienne de l’hypothèse de Riemann généralisée
venue: Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France 134(3), 417–445
read_scope: All pp.417–445, §§1–7 and bibliography. Reconstructed complex gamma phase, approximate zero jets, target pairing and fixed-block lower bound. No full external-antecedent audit. Subsequent challenge: joint phase derivative decay (12) fails; the source failure and an independent two-line Mellin replacement proof were adjudicated by the director.
main_result: Unconditional continuous lower bound with multiplicity-squared constant under complementary-function L² integrability.
selection_reason: By Mellin Plancherel and restriction to the integer reciprocal dilates, directly supplies the exact fixed-character lower bound.

title: Généralisation du critère de Beurling et Nyman pour l’hypothèse de Riemann
read_scope: §§2–4, especially Theorems 2.3, 3.2 and 4.2 and their adjacent conditions.
main_result: Qualitative continuous criterion for general series and Selberg functions; order-k smoothing for integer k>d/4.
selection_reason: Verifies the pole-cancellation, smoothing and degree conditions that separate continuous criteria from the exact norm.

title: Généralisation du critère de Beurling-Nyman pour l’hypothèse de Riemann
venue: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 359(12), 6111–6127
version: Published bibliography and HAL v1 metadata
read_scope: Crossref and author HAL record hal-00091952v1; publisher and HAL full-text downloads failed. No theorem text claimed from this version.
main_result: General continuous criterion is the stated subject; no separate theorem verification in this record.
selection_reason: Full-length version of the prior general criterion, bibliographically distinct from the 2005 short note.

title: On the mean square of the error term for an extended Selberg class
read_scope: Definitions, Theorem 2.2 and closing application to complementary-function L² integrability.
main_result: Under the weak Selberg coefficient mean-square axiom ∑_{n≤x}|a_n|²≪_εx^{1+ε}, the summatory-error mean square implies complementary-function integrability for 0<d<4.
selection_reason: Supplies the exact Hilbert-space input to the Burnol-type lower theorem for further Hecke and automorphic examples.

title: Une approche séquentielle de l’hypothèse de Riemann généralisée
version: Published bibliography and author HAL v2 metadata
read_scope: Crossref, journal abstract, and author HAL record hal-00091966v2; readable full text not retrieved. No specific rate asserted.
main_result: Author abstract states a constructed Selberg-class sequence converging under the corresponding RH.
selection_reason: Direct sequential prior-art lead for arbitrary coefficients and comparison with a fixed-character rate.

title: Zero free regions for Dirichlet series
venue: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 365(6), 3227–3253
version: Author-hosted manuscript, with arXiv and Crossref counterparts
read_scope: §2 statements and setup, including Theorems 2.1, 2.4–2.5. No complete proof audit.
main_result: A general continuous weighted criterion without an Euler-product hypothesis and a distance implication for the Dirichlet exceptional-zero problem.
selection_reason: Direct fixed-character setting, but different test space and cutoff from the discrete distance.

title: Zero-free regions for Dirichlet series (II)
version: Author-hosted manuscript, with arXiv and Crossref counterparts
read_scope: §2 setup and Corollaries 4.4–4.5 with proof and Selberg application.
main_result: Compares unconstrained and pole-cancelled continuous distances and transfers the zero-free characterization.
selection_reason: Identifies when pole constraints can be removed and what still changes in the norm and cutoff.

title: Zeros of Dirichlet polynomials via a density criterion
version: arXiv v1 (2017) inspected; publication metadata verified
read_scope: Main Theorems 1–2 and definitions; proof endpoint controlling the distinct interpolation zeros.
main_result: Fixed Dirichlet-polynomial discrete criterion at arbitrary vertical line and Burnol-type lower constant without squared multiplicity.
selection_reason: Near analogue clarifying the difference between finite Dirichlet generators and an L-function.

title: An adelic causality problem related to abelian L-functions
read_scope: §1, definitions and Theorems 1.7, 1.11, with the zeta specialization in §2 located.
main_result: Abelian RH equivalent to Hilbert-space causality and a norm-supported adelic closure.
selection_reason: Primary Hecke/abelian analogue with a different support cutoff and no ordinary coefficient rate.

title: On Fourier and Zeta(s)
read_scope: §5 theorem 5.2 and surrounding distance and vector mechanism, with §§3–4 headings and stated co-Poisson connections.
main_result: Restates the zeta multiplicity lower bound and connects zero-indexed approximate orthogonality to Fourier structure.
selection_reason: Connects the continuous lower construction with broader abelian transforms while keeping the exact scope of the distance bound.

title: Distance formulae and invariant subspaces, with an application to localization of zeros of the Riemann ζ-function
read_scope: §4 Corollaries 4.1–4.2 and their references to the invariant-subspace theorem.
main_result: Continuous Hardy-kernel distance gives a half-plane zero-free criterion and finite-subspace distances give explicit zero-free discs.
selection_reason: Underlying Hardy distance formula used in the general criteria for Dirichlet series.

title: A general strong Nyman-Beurling Criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis
read_scope: Complete 10-page arXiv v1, §§1–3 and references. Reconstructed the good-kernel hypotheses, dilation-commuting convolution, Müntz identity, and both directions of Theorem 1.2. Intermediate sign placement in §2.3 is under independent review.
main_result: For eligible smooth kernels f, RH implies approximation of f by integer dilates of its Müntz transform. For compactly supported f the reverse implication forces inclusion of right-half critical-strip zeta zeros in the zero set of the Mellin transform of f.
selection_reason: Separates a generalized target in the zeta problem from generalizing the L-function itself.
